vehicleUpdates.summary: Used petrol AWD with positive related-grade mixed-facing three-seat evidence. Budget for 12,500 km servicing and inspect early-car cooling history.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive’s 2024 S5 Sport fitted one rear-facing capsule and two forward-facing seats. Related-grade evidence for this 2.5i-L; your seats remain unconfirmed.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX positions; three rear top-tether anchors. Centre installation uses the vehicle belt.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2024 Sport: capsule behind driver plus forward-facing 0–4 and 0–8 seats; models unnamed. Earlier 2019 Premium: Unity and Graphene rear-facing, Maxi Guard Pro centre; all belted.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Daily booster buckling remains untested. ANCAP found one booster and one rear-facing convertible incompatible with the centre position, assessed individually.
familyFit.access: Related tests report generous loading access; 2023 Sport rear doors open almost 90 degrees. Try the roof-mounted centre belt.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console air vents; confirm airflow with all three restraints installed.

cons: 12,500 km service interval can require more than one visit a year at 15,000 km.
Fuel use is higher than the hybrids.
Compatible restraints fit; centre-seat restrictions and booster buckles still need a personal trial.
inspection: Read the build plate: late-2021 MY22 facelift cars differ from MY21.
Ask for dated 12,500 km service invoices, coolant history and any thermo-control-valve diagnosis/replacement.
Road test the CVT cold and warm; ask a Subaru specialist to diagnose warnings, shudder or leaks.
Load-test the 12 V battery and test air-conditioning, EyeSight, cameras and every restraint buckle.
Check MY23 REC-005831 / SRT-352 driveshaft recall completion by VIN; applicable rectification is free.
Trial your rear-facing seat at its required recline, two other restraints, all buckles and your normal driving positions.
gaps: Exact 2.5i-L restraint models, booster access and your fit are unconfirmed.
Price sample is small, spans 2021/2023 years, kilometres and fee bases.
No representative Australian annual repair average or exact installed CVT quote verified.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive’s S6 Hybrid Sport fitted two forward-facing seats plus a rear-facing seat behind the driver. Related powertrain/grade; confirm in the petrol base.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX positions and three rear top tethers. No centre ISOFIX pair.
familyFit.testedSeats: July 2025 S6 Hybrid Sport: two forward-facing plus one rear-facing behind driver. Restraint models unnamed.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Booster buckle access untested; ANCAP found one tested booster incompatible with the rear centre position. Individual position testing does not prove three across.
familyFit.access: July mixed-seat test allowed a 186 cm driver; separate preview with a 0–4 rear-facing convertible allowed 180 cm. Clearance depends on the seat and recline.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console air vents, documented in the new-generation family test and Australian specification.

ownershipUpdates.serviceInterval: S5/MY21–MY24: 12 months or 12,500 km. S6/MY26: 12 months or 15,000 km. Whichever first.
ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE: A$750/year for the used S5 at 15,000 km/year, including post-cap uncertainty (A$600–1,100). Historical first-five caps: MY21 A$2,413.63; MY24 A$2,674.64, each over 62,500 km, not five years at this mileage. They are not current used-car quotations. MY21 handbook normally inspects CVT oil; extreme-condition work needs the workshop schedule. Excludes repairs and tyres.
warrantyCautions: Private-use manufacturer cover is five years / unlimited kilometres from original supply, not from your used-car purchase. Commercial/hire/ride-share uses have a 150,000 km limit; check the contract.
Dealer-backed extended warranties can have conditions and are separate from Subaru’s manufacturer warranty. Do not assume a photographed or advertised ten-year dealer scheme applies.
Australian Consumer Law rights are separate from the written warranty; ask for the VIN-specific warranty and recall status.
The October 2026 REC-006737 parking-pawl campaign is for 42 selected Forester Hybrid VINs. It is not assigned to this petrol S6 configuration.
Original warranty and eligible capped servicing transfer with the vehicle; original start date, remaining time/kilometres and exclusions still apply. A 2021 car may now be out of manufacturer cover.
S5 12 V starter battery cover is two years under the applicable handbook, shorter than the five-year vehicle warranty. Verify the original booklet and S6 VIN-specific exclusions.

risks.title: CVT / AWD drivetrain inspection
risks.detail: A major gearbox or engine repair can exceed a small annual reserve. Inspect cold and hot operation, leaks, warnings and service invoices. No representative Australian failure rate for these exact configurations was found.
risks.priceBasis: Unpriced: no exact Australian installed quote verified. Obtain a VIN-specific diagnosis and written parts/labour/GST quote; do not transfer prices or failure rates from older Subarus.
risks.warranty: Manufacturing-defect cover depends on the original warranty, diagnosis, service history and exclusions; wear and external damage differ.

risks.title: Early S5 thermo-control valve: diagnosis and support check
risks.detail: US bulletin covers 2019–2021 Forester coolant-valve sensor intrusion and a revised component. Relevant inspection lead for an early S5, not proof every Australian VIN or the S6 is affected. Australian installed pricing and incidence remain unverified.
risks.priceBasis: Unpriced: an Australian installed repair quote and incidence were not verified. Ask for diagnostic codes and any replacement invoice.
risks.warranty: The US 15-year / 150,000-mile extension is not an Australian warranty entitlement. Ask Subaru Australia to confirm VIN-specific support before paying.

risks.title: MY23 S5 driveshaft recall: free VIN-specific remedy
risks.detail: REC-005831 / SRT-352 covers 186 vehicles across MY23 Forester, MY23 Outback and MY24 Crosstrek. A front driveshaft outer race may crack, stopping the vehicle. Check the actual VIN; this is not an S6 campaign.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for applicable official recall rectification; not a predicted paid repair.
risks.warranty: Recall remedy is free and separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

forester-awd-petrol-2025.serviceBasis: Australian MY26 S6 petrol capped visits: A$347.95,520.45,393.10,679.30 and 358.20 = A$2,299 for first five services / five years / 75,000 km; A$459.80/year at 15,000 km/year. Includes GST. Post-cap years and additional work are not quoted; the upper bound is a planning allowance. The generic Subaru website still mentions 12,500 km for Forester; the model-specific MY26 PDF explicitly supersedes it with 15,000 km.

fuelEstimate.basis: L/100 km family-driving scenario for S5 petrol: 8.5 point, 7.4–11 sensitivity bounds. CarExpert’s related 2021 2.5i-S observed consumption in the middle eights in mixed urban/highway use; ADR combined 7.4. This is one higher-trim test plus analyst bounds, not a fleet mean.

forester-awd-petrol-2025.basis: L/100 km planning point 9.3 uses CarExpert’s related S6 Touring petrol mixed-route indicated test; base petrol AWD may differ. ADR combined 7.9; 7.9–11.5 are analyst sensitivity bounds, not confidence limits or a measured fleet average.

reviewUpdates.scope: ProductReview S5 generation page only; mixed grades, petrol/hybrid labels, years and possible incorrectly categorised reports. Excludes S6. Self-selected opinions, not a reliability survey.
reviewUpdates.summary: S5 aggregate 3.1/5 from 57. Exact 2.5i-L subpage shows 3.5/5 from 11 but contains older/mistagged reports; do not combine counts or treat either as a 2021–2024-only result.
positiveThemes: Space, visibility, comfort and AWD usefulness.
negativeThemes: Some owners report cooling-valve, air-conditioning/starting and warranty-service frustrations. No failure frequency can be inferred.

arrangement.detail: 2024 S5 Sport fitted a rear-facing capsule behind the driver plus forward-facing 0–4 and 0–8 seats. Named models unavailable.

buckles.detail: Daily buckling with boosters was not demonstrated. Centre-position compatibility varies; ANCAP rejects one tested booster and one rear-facing convertible.

space.detail: 184 cm driver fitted ahead of the capsule in the 2024 trial. A different rear-facing convertible may require more room.

access.detail: Related Sport testing found wide rear-door opening and easy child loading.

fitAssessments.summary: S6 Hybrid Sport demonstrates the facing mix; the petrol base is related evidence.

buckles.detail: No occupied three-restraint booster-buckling trial. ANCAP rejects one selected centre booster, tested alone.

space.detail: July mixed-seat trial allowed a 186 cm driver. Preview with a different 0–4 rear-facing convertible allowed 180 cm; recline and model affect clearance.

access.detail: Rear anchor access is documented, but a specific petrol-base child-loading and door-clearance trial was not verified.

audit.summary: Both generations have positive related-grade one-rear-facing/two-forward-facing evidence. Added centre-restraint caveats and MY23 driveshaft recall; retained honest repair uncertainty.
